missing_evidence: No PO amendment, change order, or written authorization is present to explain why INV-1004 (82,500) exceeds the originally issued PO-1004 value (75,000).

No reconciliation document exists explaining why REC-1004 states an accepted value of 75,000 (matching the original PO) while the invoice, bank statement, and ledger all reflect 82,500 — i.e., no evidence that the higher amount was ever formally accepted.
notes: All five expected document types for a standard purchase-to-pay cycle (purchase order, invoice, receipt, bank statement, ledger entry) are present and cross-reference one another, so the transaction is structurally complete. However, the amounts are internally inconsistent: PO-1004 and REC-1004 agree on 75,000, while INV-1004, BNK-1004, and LED-1004 agree on 82,500. The presence of a successful bank payment and matching ledger entry at 82,500 does not establish that the higher amount was properly authorized or that the receipt's stated acceptance value was superseded — only a document such as a PO amendment or updated acceptance/receipt would establish that. Because the receipt (the document meant to confirm accepted value/quantity) does not match the amount actually invoiced and paid, and no supplementary authorization document is present, confidence in this transaction being fully and correctly supported is low-to-moderate.
